d: a division or group based upon different doctrinal opinions and/or loyalties and hence by implication in certain contexts an unjustified party or group (applicable in the NT to religious parties)
(derivative of {L:ἔθνος<SDBG:ἔθνος:000000>} ‘nation,’ {D:11.55}) pertaining to one who is not a Jew
(derivative of {L:ἔθνος<SDBG:ἔθνος:000000>} ‘nation,’ {D:11.55}) pertaining to being like or similar to one who is not a Jew
(an extended meaning of {L:ἔθνος<SDBG:ἔθνος:000000>} ‘nation,’ {D:11.55}) those who do not belong to the Jewish or Christian faith
a congregation of Christians, implying interacting membership
(an idiom, literally: sons of this age) persons who hold to the value system of the world
(an extended meaning of {L:Ἕλλην<SDBG:Ἕλλην:000000>}[a] ‘Greek,’ {D:11.90}) a person who is a Gentile in view of being a Greek
(an extended meaning of {L:Ἑλληνίς<SDBG:Ἑλληνίς:000000>}[a] ‘Greek woman,’ {D:11.91}) a female who is a Gentile in view of being a Greek
(an idiom, literally: to have someone’s name called upon someone) to be acknowledged as belonging to the one whose name is called upon such an individual
a state of being uncircumcised by not having the foreskin of the penis cut off{N:001}
a class or division of persons who perform certain daily duties (in the one NT occurrence, a reference to a group of priests performing certain functions in the Temple at Jerusalem)
a person not belonging to the ethnic group in question (from the specifically Jewish point of view, one who is not a Jew, but a Gentile)
a collective for people who belong to God (whether Jews or Christians)
(a figurative extension of meaning of νεόφυτος ‘newly planted,’ not occurring in the NT) an individual who has recently become a member of a religious group
a member of a well-defined socio-religious entity and representing an older age group than the so-called reference person
persons who belong to God, and as such constitute a religious entity

g: those of the circumcision or those who insisted on circumcision
d: (a set phrase, literally: those of circumcision) those who insisted on circumcising Gentiles if they were to be regarded as true believers in Jesus Christ
one (female) who is included among the faithful followers of Christ

g: people who are like a flock
d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ποίμνη<SDBG:ποίμνη:000000>}[a] ‘flock,’ {D:4.28}) the followers of Christ constituting a well-defined membership group

g: people who are like a flock
d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ποίμνιον ‘flock,’ not occurring in the NT) the followers of Christ constituting a well-defined membership group

g: a person who is like a sheep
d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:πρόβατον<SDBG:πρόβατον:000000>}[a] ‘sheep,’ {D:4.22}) a follower of Christ, with the implication of needing care and guidance
a Gentile who had converted to Judaism

a member of a politically influential Jewish party in Jerusalem at the time of Jesus and the apostles. The Sadducees were a smaller group than the Pharisees (see {D:11.49}), but were often in control of important political and religious positions. Their denial of the resurrection of the dead and their acceptance of only the first five books of the OT are important elements in some of the important differences which arose between the Sadducees and the Pharisees
a non-Jew who lives completely without reference to the Jewish Law
an assembled group of worshipers or members of such a group
(a figurative extension of meaning of σῶμα[a] ‘body,’ {D:8.1}) believers in Christ who are joined together as a group, with the implication of each having a distinctive function within the group
(an idiom, literally: children of light) persons to whom the truth of God has been revealed and who are presumably living according to such truth. See also {D:9.4} and {D:12.15}
one who is initiated into a religious community of faith (a meaning which reflects the occurrence of τέλειος as a technical term for persons initiated into the mystery religions)
(an idiom, literally: sons of the kingdom) people who should properly be or were traditionally regarded as a part of the kingdom of God

a member of an important religious and political Jewish party at the time of Jesus and the apostles. The Pharisees constituted a significantly larger group than the Sadducees (see {D:11.48}) and differed with them on certain doctrines and patterns of behavior. The Pharisees were strict and jealous adherents to the laws of the OT and to numerous additional traditions
(a set phrase, literally: the twelve tribes, but used in a figurative sense) all of the people of God as a possible reference to the new Israel

(idioms, literally: sons of the light, and: children of light, respectively) persons to whom the truth of God has been revealed and who are presumably living according to such truth. See also {D:9.4} and {D:12.15}
one who is identified as a believer in and follower of Christ
an individual who pretends to be a close member of a socio-religious group but is not (see {D:11.22}, {D:11.23}, and {D:11.24})
a person who does not belong to the group of believers in Christ{N:001}
a state of having been excommunicated from membership in a synagogue

g: a person who is like a lamb
d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀρνίον<SDBG:ἀρνίον:000000>}[a] ‘lamb,’ {D:4.25}) a follower of Christ, with the implication of helplessness and dependence
a close female associate of a group with well-defined membership (in the NT referring specifically to fellow believers in Christ)
a close associate of a group of persons having a well-defined membership (in the NT ἀδελφός[b] refers specifically to fellow believers in Christ)
an association of persons having a strong sense of unity
a person who is not a member of the Christian community and by implication possibly unjust or not in a right relation with God
